browserChecks: Selecting one saved tab opens only that URL; all three saved tabs remain stored
Global title search finds a page in another collection; clicking its collection reveals and expands it
Empty collections remain discoverable by name
Editing notes creates a recovery point containing the original data
Cancelling recovery leaves the edited notes unchanged
Confirming recovery restores old notes, captures the replaced state, and neither opens nor closes tabs
Opening a twelve-tab collection requires confirmation and initially opens five tabs
Cancelling during the batch pause keeps the number of opened tabs at five; twelve tabs remain stored
Newly opened tabs share a recreated group with the stored title, color and collapsed state
Compact density persists in Chrome storage and reduced a sample narrow-screen card from about 242px to 214px
No horizontal overflow at 390px and no console errors in the final search check
automatedValidation: 39 automated tests; production build and strict TypeScript checks for changed modules
limitations: Chrome API behavior was exercised through mocks; native group creation in an installed Chrome extension was not manually exercised.
Batching reduces bursts of page creation but does not guarantee low memory use after all pages are opened.
